_comment: Nova security findings registry. Managed by security subagent. Do NOT edit manually unless you know what you are doing.

findings.title: GET /api/config returns raw API credentials
findings.detail: The GET /api/config endpoint returns the plaintext APCA_API_KEY_ID and APCA_API_SECRET_KEY values to any caller with network access. This leaks broker credentials to any authenticated or unauthenticated client that can reach the API port.
findings.compensating_controls: Local-first Productization-Decision; alerts module already has mask_secret pattern; no remote auth assumed for single-operator desktop.
findings.acceptance_rationale: GET /api/config returns api_key_masked/api_secret_masked + *_set flags; plaintext removed (health.py).

findings.title: Executor POST routes have no authentication guard
findings.detail: backend/routes/executor.py exposes 9 POST routes including arm, kill-switch, disarm, flatten, approve/reject staged tickets — none of which use a FastAPI Depends() authentication guard. Any network client can trigger executor state changes without credentials.
findings.redacted_evidence: 9 POST route(s); no Depends(...) auth guard found
findings.compensating_controls: FLATTEN typed confirm token; IBKR_ENABLED + IBKR_ORDERS_ENABLED + IBKR_LIVE_TRADING_CONFIRMED gates in ibkr/safety.py; auto_live hard-rejected in control_mode.py; local-first.
findings.acceptance_rationale: Executor POSTs use Depends(require_auth); MutatingApiKeyMiddleware covers /api/* mutations.

findings.title: CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS_DEFAULT is set to wildcard ["*"]
findings.detail: backend/constants_scanner.py sets CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS_DEFAULT = ["*"], which allows any web origin to make cross-origin requests to the API. backend/constants.py is a compatibility barrel (`from constants_scanner import *`, Phase 3 constants split) and only re-exports this value — it is not independently redefined there, so the centralized-constants "import, don't re-declare" policy is followed correctly. This is acceptable in pure local-dev, but becomes a high-risk misconfiguration if the API is deployed to Railway without setting NOVA_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS in the env.
findings.compensating_controls: allow_credentials=False; NOVA_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS env override documented; intended for localhost Vite. Superseded fingerprint 8f87c08a53f3ca5b3a70b87726b3b6593a06078ce0f7ac131cb06f9fb297514a (old location backend/constants.py:34, pre-Phase-3-split) folded in here 2026-07-16 — same single value, not a second instance; see run log for SEC-007 dedup analysis.

findings.title: No API authentication middleware found in backend
findings.detail: No FastAPI auth patterns (APIKeyHeader, HTTPBearer, OAuth2, or a global Depends with a known auth guard name) were found across the backend Python files. All API routes are effectively unauthenticated, including sensitive /api/config, /api/strategy/executor, and /api/trading endpoints.
findings.compensating_controls: Same as SEC-002 IBKR spend gates; product is single-operator local API; Electron sidecar binds 127.0.0.1.

findings.title: CI deploy.yml missing security scan jobs: gitleaks, osv-scanner, semgrep
findings.detail: The GitHub Actions workflow at .github/workflows/deploy.yml does not include jobs for: gitleaks, osv-scanner, semgrep. Secret leaks and known-vulnerable dependencies can reach production undetected. Add gitleaks, osv-scanner, and semgrep steps before the deploy job.
findings.compensating_controls: security-audit CI job now runs tools/security_audit.py with continue-on-error; .env gitignored; pip-audit available via requirements-dev.
findings.acceptance_rationale: deploy.yml adds gitleaks, osv-scanner, and semgrep jobs (warning-only).

findings.title: Dockerfile runs container process as root (no USER directive)
findings.detail: Root Dockerfile has no USER directive, so uvicorn runs as UID 0. A container escape or path-traversal bug would yield root privileges. Add a non-root user before CMD.
findings.redacted_evidence: No USER directive found before CMD
findings.compensating_controls: Railway may remap UIDs; no --privileged; still should add USER.
findings.acceptance_rationale: Dockerfile creates non-root user nova (UID 10001) and USER before CMD.

findings.title: torch 2.10.0 known CVEs (PYSEC-2026-139, PYSEC-2025-194)
findings.detail: pip_audit reports two known vulnerabilities in torch==2.10.0 (pinned in backend/requirements.txt): PYSEC-2026-139 (local deserialization via pt2 Loading Handler; no Fix Versions listed) and PYSEC-2025-194 / CVE-2025-3000 (torch.jit.script memory corruption; Fix Versions include 2.13.0; NVD CVSS 3.1 ~5.3). Torch is pulled for FinBERT via transformers in news/sentiment.py. Both CVEs are local-attack-vector; still expands container attack surface on Railway Dockerfile installs.
findings.compensating_controls: FinBERT load is lazy and fails soft; no remote model-upload path; attack requires local code/file control on the API host.
findings.acceptance_rationale: torch/transformers removed from requirements.txt; optional requirements-ml.txt with torch>=2.13.

findings.title: Unauthenticated SSRF via alerts webhook channels
findings.detail: POST /api/alerts/channels accepts an arbitrary webhook_url with no auth (see SEC-004) and no URL allowlist / private-IP block. POST /api/alerts/test then causes the server to urllib.request.urlopen that URL (alerts/generic_webhook.py / discord.py). On a networked or cloud-deployed API this is classic SSRF (probe localhost, link-local metadata, internal hosts).
findings.compensating_controls: Local-first / 127.0.0.1 Electron bind; webhook URLs masked in list responses (mask_secret); still no egress allowlist.
findings.acceptance_rationale: alerts/webhook_url.py validates https + blocks private/link-local/metadata; enforced on create/send.

scan_runs.summary: Security subagent re-audit: run_builtin_checks() empty; open_finding_count 0; SEC-001–08 remain fixed; spot-checks auth/config-mask/webhook/Docker USER/CI scanners/no-torch pass; IBKR+auto_live gates intact.
Parent remediation closed SEC-001–SEC-008. Builtin checks clean; torch optional; webhook SSRF validator + API key middleware.

Full posture audit (Daddy dispatch). Deterministic scan reconfirmed SEC-001–006 (0 new from nova-builtin). Complementary: pip_audit found torch 2.10.0 CVEs (SEC-007); manual SSRF triage on alerts webhooks (SEC-008). npm audit clean (0 vulns). ruff: 3 non-security hygiene issues only. No committed .env (only .env.example). IBKR spend gates intact in ibkr/safety.py + execution/validate.py; auto_live still rejected. Trading POST /order unauth covered by SEC-004 (not a new ID).

Manual dedup: dry-run `py -3 tools/security_audit.py --json` (registry not written) surfaced a candidate SEC-007 for CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS_DEFAULT at backend/constants_scanner.py:34, same title/CVSS as SEC-003. Verified with grep/Read: backend/constants.py is a Phase 3 compatibility barrel (`from constants_scanner import *`) and no longer contains the literal at line 34 (file is 19 lines, barrel-only) — the value is defined exactly once, in constants_scanner.py. No centralized-constants violation. Root cause of the false duplicate: normalize.fingerprint() hashes (source, kind, path, title), so a constants-module split changes the fingerprint even though the finding is the same logical issue. Folded the new fingerprint into SEC-003 (location + fingerprint updated to constants_scanner.py:34) instead of creating SEC-007. Did not use `--write-registry` because its merge_findings() only dedupes by exact fingerprint match and would have added SEC-007 as a second open finding rather than recognizing the relocation.
